parts.zh: 苏格兰一座16世纪的城堡在洪水冲走大块土壤后濒临倒塌
位于苏格兰阿伯丁郡的阿伯geldie城堡由米德马尔的亚历山大·戈登爵士建造
负责投递和邮局运营的副总裁Dean Granholm表示
W: 但这是很简单的事啊
M: 但问题是这个人8点钟就打过卡了
W: 你跟那个迟到的人谈过了吗?
M: 还没有。我想先跟您谈谈
W: 那你想让我做什么?
M: 我在想您能不能见见Smith——就是那个迟到的人——因为您处理这类事情要在行得多

items.stem: Why did John Gordon move out of Abergeldie Castle?

choices.text: It was dangerous to live in.
It was going to be renovated.
He could no longer pay the rent.
He had sold it to the royal family.
choices.zh: 他已经把它卖给了王室。

items.stem: What happened in Scotland last Wednesday?

choices.text: A strike.
A storm.
A forest fire.
A terrorist attack.

items.stem: What does the news report say about the salt miners?

choices.text: They lost contact with the emergency department.
choices.zh: 他们与应急部门失去了联系。

choices.text: They were trapped in an underground elevator.
choices.zh: 他们被困在地下电梯里。

choices.text: They were injured by suddenly falling rocks.
choices.zh: 他们被突然落下的岩石砸伤。

choices.text: They sent calls for help via a portable radio.
choices.zh: 他们通过便携式无线电发送了求救信号。

items.stem: What did the rescue team do?

choices.text: They tried hard to repair the elevator.
They released the details of the accident.
choices.zh: 他们公布了事故的详细情况。

choices.text: They sent supplies to keep the miners warm.
choices.zh: 他们送去了供给品以保持矿工温暖。

choices.text: They provided the miners with food and water.
choices.zh: 他们为矿工提供了食物和水。

items.stem: What is the U.S. Postal Service planning to do?

choices.text: Raise postage rates.
Improve its services.
Redesign delivery routes.
Close some of its post offices.

items.stem: What measure has been planned to save costs?

choices.text: Shortening business hours.
Closing offices on holidays.
choices.zh: 在节假日关闭办公场所。

choices.text: Stopping mail delivery on Saturdays.
Computerizing mall sorting processes.
choices.zh: 将邮件分拣过程电脑化。

items.stem: What will happen when the proposed measure comes into effect?

choices.text: Many post office staff will lose their jobs.
choices.zh: 许多邮局员工将失去工作。

choices.text: Many people will begin to complain.
Taxpayers will be very pleased.
A lot of controversy will arise.

items.stem: What will happen to the press operator who was late for work according to the woman?

choices.text: He will be kept from promotion.
He will go through retraining.
He will be given a warning.
He will lose part of his pay.

items.stem: What does the man say about John who stands by the time clock?

choices.text: He is always on time.
He is a trustworthy guy.
choices.zh: 他是一个值得信赖的人。

choices.text: He is an experienced press operator.
choices.zh: 他是一名经验丰富的印刷机操作员。

choices.text: He is on good terms with his workmates.

items.stem: Why does the man suggest the woman see the worker who was late?

choices.text: She is a trade union representative.
She is in charge of public relations.
She is a senior manager of the shop.
choices.zh: 她是车间的高级管理人员。

choices.text: She is better at handling such matters.
choices.zh: 她更擅长处理此类事务。

items.stem: What does the woman say about Jack Green?

choices.text: He is skilled and experienced.
choices.zh: 他技术熟练且经验丰富。

choices.text: He is very close to the manager.
He is always trying to stir up trouble.
He is always complaining about low wages.

items.stem: What do foreigners generally think of British people according to the woman?

choices.text: Open.
Friendly.
Selfish.
Reserved.

items.stem: What may British people typically do on a train according to the man?

choices.text: They stay quiet.
They read a book.
They talk about the weather.
They chat with fellow passengers.

items.stem: What does the man say about the Italian woman working in Manchester?

choices.text: She was always treated as a foreigner.
choices.zh: 她总是被当作外国人对待

choices.text: She was eager to visit an English castle.
She was never invited to a colleague's home.
choices.zh: 她从未被邀请去同事家里

choices.text: She was unwilling to make friends with workmates.
choices.zh: 她不愿意与同事交朋友

items.stem: Why do British people prefer houses to flats?

choices.text: Houses are much more quiet.
Houses provide more privacy.
They want to have more space.
They want a garden of their own.
choices.zh: 他们想要有自己的花园

items.stem: What does the speaker say about college students applying for on-campus jobs?

choices.text: They don't have much choice of jobs.
choices.zh: 他们没有太多工作选择。

choices.text: They are likely to get much higher pay.
choices.zh: 他们有可能获得更高的薪水。

choices.text: They don't have to go through job interviews.
choices.zh: 他们不必经过求职面试。

choices.text: They will automatically be given hiring priority.
choices.zh: 他们将自动获得招聘优先权。

items.stem: What can students do to find a campus job according to the speaker?

choices.text: Ask their professors for help.
choices.zh: 向他们的教授寻求帮助。

choices.text: Look at school bulletin boards.
Visit the school careers service.
choices.zh: 访问学校就业服务中心。

choices.text: Go through campus newspapers.

items.stem: What does the speaker say is a library monitor's responsibility?

choices.text: Helping students find the books and journals they need.
choices.zh: 帮助学生找到他们需要的书籍和期刊。

choices.text: Supervising study spaces to ensure a quiet atmosphere.
choices.zh: 监督自习空间以确保安静的氛围。

choices.text: Helping students arrange appointments with librarians.
choices.zh: 帮助学生安排与图书馆员的预约。

choices.text: Providing students with information about the library.
choices.zh: 向学生提供有关图书馆的信息。

items.stem: Why have tea farmers in Kenya decided to grow purple tea?

choices.text: It tastes better.
It is easier to grow.
It may be sold at a higher price.
choices.zh: 可能以更高的价格出售。

choices.text: It can better survive extreme weathers.
choices.zh: 能更好地在极端天气中存活。

items.stem: What do researchers say about purple tea?

choices.text: It is healthier than green tea.
It can grow in drier soil.
choices.zh: 它能在更干旱的土壤中生长。

choices.text: It will replace green tea one day.
choices.zh: 它总有一天会取代绿茶。

choices.text: It is immune to various diseases.

items.stem: What has Mr. Kibara found about purple tea?

choices.text: It has been well received by many tea drinkers.
choices.zh: 它受到了许多饮茶者的欢迎。

choices.text: It does not bring the promised health benefits.
choices.zh: 它没有带来所承诺的健康益处。

choices.text: It has made tea farmers' life easier.
choices.zh: 它使茶农的生活更轻松了。

choices.text: It does not have a stable market.

items.stem: What does the speaker say about today's consumers?

choices.text: They need decorations to show their status.
choices.zh: 他们需要装饰品来显示自己的地位。

choices.text: They prefer unique objects of high quality.
choices.zh: 他们更喜欢高质量的独特物品。

choices.text: They decorate their homes themselves.
They care more about environment.

items.stem: What does the speaker say about good craftsmen in the past?

choices.text: They were proud of their creations.
choices.zh: 他们为自己的作品感到自豪。

choices.text: They could only try to create at night.
choices.zh: 他们只能在夜间尝试进行创作。

choices.text: They made great contributions to society.
choices.zh: 他们为社会做出了巨大贡献。

choices.text: They focused on the quality of their products.

items.stem: What do craftsmen help consumers do?

choices.text: Make wise choices.
Identify fake crafts.
Design handicrafts themselves.
Learn the importance of creation.

items.stem: Why do state art councils help sponsor local arts and crafts festivals?

choices.text: To boost the local economy.
To attract foreign investments.
To arouse public interest in crafts.
choices.zh: 唤起公众对工艺品的兴趣。

choices.text: To preserve the traditional culture.
